_maintained_by: Authored from the spec: each golden preimage and hash comes from an encoder written independently of both implementations. The Go (senderauth/deposit_request_v2.go) and TypeScript (sender-auth/src/deposit-request-v2.ts) implementations both read this file, so every vector here must hold in both, with the same refusal detail. Each request is the raw JSON text, so a vector can carry bytes a parsed object cannot (duplicate or case-twin members). preimage is the exact keccak256 input; check want with `cast keccak <preimage>`, and wantV1 with `cast keccak <request_id>`. Each reencoded row is a golden request as an honest path between payer and reader re-encoded it, produced by running that path's own code (go-schemajson: the generated SchemaJson decode and json.Marshal solver-gw runs; settler-zod-jcs: the settler's zod parse and RFC 8785 JCS on the Quote API flow, settler-agent f9c957de schema; postgres-jsonb: a jsonb column written and read back as text on postgres:17, as payment-gw stores payment_request_json), and must keep the golden's v1 and v2. Every golden has one row per path, except the pairs reencodedGaps names, each with the reason that path never re-encodes it. The SECTEST-497 rows rebuild that issue's twin/variant table against this file's base request. If a case fails, reconcile the implementations against the vector; do not edit the expectation to match the code.
